distractors.reason: We don't say 'rate loudly'. 'Loudly' describes sound, as in speak loudly or shout loudly.
We don't say 'rate quickly' in this sense. 'Quickly' describes speed, as in work quickly.
We don't say 'rate heavily'. 'Heavily' describes weight or large amounts, as in rain heavily.

example_sentence: Critics rated the new film ___ because the acting was excellent.
l1_interference: В українській мові прислівник часто стоїть перед дієсловом, тому носії можуть сказати «highly rate» замість правильного «rate highly». В англійській мові прислівник зазвичай стоїть після дієслова.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb: rate highly, listen carefully, work hard. Here 'highly' means 'with a good opinion'. The other adverbs do not combine with 'rate' in this sense.

related_collocations.example: Listen carefully before you write your review.
The actors worked hard on the film.
I always sleep well after a good book.

memory_tip: ADVERB GOES AFTER THE VERB: rate highly, listen carefully, work hard | 'highly rate' is wrong
